additional_gap_in_proposed_no_saturation.issue: A globally strict safe tuple t may project into S|E on the old block E where the target obstruction remains. Theorem 5.3 localizes target failure, but does not guarantee that t|E is a strict local extension.
additional_gap_in_proposed_no_saturation.consequence: Pure block enumeration without a strictness detector is insufficient for the existing local SAFEEXT solver.

v0_4_repair.name: STRICT_EXISTENTIAL_OLD_BLOCK_LOCALIZATION_V1
method: enumerate all old y-failing large BMS blocks E
if S<T_E, extract an immediate global safe witness from T_E\S
if S=T_E, strictness of every global t outside S is visible on E; run the strict liftable d-coherent SAFEEXT solver
completeness: a global safe t yields a failing post-extension block U; refinement gives U subset E for an old block; y_E is excluded from Sg(S_E,t_E); split on S<T_E versus S=T_E
v0_4_repair.forbidden_old_claim: No claim remains that global SAFEEXT is equivalent to local SAFEEXT on one preselected E.
